moments.title: The parade leaves Wrigley Field
moments.text: Two days after the Cubs won their first World Series since 1908, the team's parade left Wrigley Field for downtown on a route of several miles lined with fans.

moments.title: The rally in Grant Park
moments.text: The parade ended at a rally in Grant Park, where the team celebrated the title with fans.

moments.title: An estimated 5 million
moments.text: City officials put the total crowd along the route and at the rally at about 5 million. No independent count was made, and parade crowd estimates are hard to verify.

moments.title: Today: Hutchinson Field
moments.text: Hutchinson Field is an open lawn in Grant Park again.

facts.label: Crowd
facts.note: The figure came from city officials; it was never independently counted.

facts.label: Title drought ended
facts.note: The Cubs' previous title was in 1908.

sources.title: City estimates 5 million people attend Cubs World Series parade (CBS Sports)
Cubs fans celebrate World Series crown with parade, rally (Associated Press via ABC7)

checked.notes: Date Nov 4, 2016 and the city's 5 million estimate confirmed (CBS Sports, AP). Route length is reported as 6 or 7 miles, so it is given as 'several miles'. No source found with a specific alternative count; Sports Business Daily quotes a producer saying parade estimates are 'always dicey'. The story's 'a number crowd experts have questioned' was reworded to say the figure was never independently counted. Game 7 details (Nov 2 in Cleveland) and the Hutchinson Field location were not separately confirmed (search budget ran out); both are left as written. The 108-year drought (last title 1908) comes from the existing story and was not separately confirmed.
